measured_over: 8 sub-millimetre shifts of the whole scene along y (realisations of EEVEE's dither), 64 by 64 frame, 16 samples, 9 by 9 patch mean. Potter's realtime render of the same scenes (the same shifts) gave patch means identical to 1e-8 at every shift.

BLENDED.derivation: EEVEE's value is constant across all 8 shifts (sigma 0). The EXR is half-float; for values in [0.5, 1) the rounding error is at most 2^-12 = 0.000244140625. Potter's realtime output is exact (sigma 0), so the tolerance is that rounding bound alone.

DITHERED.derivation: The expectation is the channel mean of the Transparent Color, (0.2 + 0.8 + 0.4) / 3. Potter asserts that expectation to f32 storage (tolerance 1e-5). EEVEE's dithered mean sits 0.00956 above it, 13 standard errors (sigma 0.00207 over 8 shifts), so the offset is systematic, not noise. Mechanism, from source: the depth prepass discards a fragment when average(T) > threshold (eevee_surf_depth.bsl.hh 76-85), where threshold is the Wyman-McGuire hashed alpha test on the fragment position with alpha_hash_scale 0.1 for final renders (eevee_transparency.bsl.hh; eevee_pipeline.cc 781), jittered per sample by a base-7 Halton value at sample+1 (eevee_sampling.cc 194). The film then sums the samples with a Gaussian fit to Blackman-Harris of radius 1.5 (eevee_film_shared.hh 129; eevee_film.cc 745-800), with sub-pixel jitter from base-2/3 Halton (eevee_film.cc 680-705). A model with those rules (tests run offline, not in Potter) gives 0.4785 over the same 8 shifts, 0.0022 above EEVEE, within the derived tolerance for the model. Without the film filter the same hash model gives 0.4871, which is ruled out. Potter's realtime sampler averages uniform samples and does not splat them through EEVEE's filter, so matching this needs a sampler change for every realtime surface, not a DITHERED-only tolerance.
